_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a real drill sentence from that point. 'nonstandard': entries hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.point: Present-tense verbs change with gender and number
entries.label: Present (pa'al)
entries.usage: Four forms for one tense: הולך, הולכת, הולכים, הולכות.
entries.example: היא הולכת הביתה. — She is going home.

entries.point: Past tense pa'al: the singular persons
entries.label: Past (pa'al sg.)
entries.usage: Endings, not prefixes: כתבתי, כתבת, כתב, כתבה.
entries.example: אתמול כתבתי מכתב. — Yesterday I wrote a letter.

entries.point: Past tense pa'al: the plural persons
entries.label: Past (pa'al pl.)
entries.usage: כתבנו for we, כתבתם for you, and one כתבו for they.
entries.example: הם אכלו פיצה. — They ate pizza.

entries.label: Future (pa'al)
entries.usage: Prefixes take over: א for I, ת for you, י for he, נ for we.
entries.example: מחר אכתוב מכתב. — Tomorrow I will write a letter.

entries.label: Infinitive
entries.usage: The ל־ form that never changes, whoever the subject is.
entries.example: אני רוצה ללכת הביתה. — I want to go home.

entries.point: Roots and binyanim: how the system works
entries.label: Root & binyan
entries.usage: One root, seven patterns: לובש, מלביש, מתלבש.
entries.example: אני מתלבש מהר בבוקר. — I get dressed quickly in the morning.

entries.label: Present (pi'el)
entries.usage: מ־ plus an a-vowel: מדבר, מלמד, מבקש.
entries.example: היא מדברת עברית. — She speaks Hebrew.

entries.point: Pi'el in the past and the future
entries.label: Pi'el past/future
entries.usage: The מ־ drops away: דיברתי, דיבר, אדבר, ידברו.
entries.example: אתמול דיברתי עם המנהל. — Yesterday I spoke with the manager.

entries.label: Present (hif'il)
entries.usage: מ־ plus an i-vowel: מרגיש, מתחיל, מסביר.
entries.example: אני מרגיש טוב היום. — I feel good today.

entries.point: Hif'il in the past and the future
entries.label: Hif'il past/future
entries.usage: ה־ in the past (הרגיש), ordinary prefixes in the future (ירגיש).
entries.example: המורה הסביר את הכלל. — The teacher explained the rule.

entries.label: Hitpa'el
entries.usage: מת־ in the present, הת־ in the past; the ת can swap places.
entries.example: הוא השתמש במילון. — He used a dictionary.

entries.point: Nif'al: the middle and passive pattern
entries.label: Nif'al
entries.usage: נ־ throughout: נכנס, נפגשים, נשברה — things that happen to the subject.
entries.example: הכוס נשברה. — The glass broke.

entries.point: Pu'al and huf'al: recognizing the passives
entries.label: Pu'al & huf'al
entries.usage: Passive-only patterns with an u-vowel: בוטלה, מסודר, מוזמן, הופסק.
entries.example: הטיסה בוטלה. — The flight was cancelled.

entries.label: Binyan idioms
entries.usage: Same root, unpredictable meaning: ראה, הראה, נראה, נשבר לי.
entries.example: אתה נראה עייף היום. — You look tired today.

entries.point: The vav-conversive in quotation and idiom
entries.label: Vav-conversive
entries.usage: Biblical tense-flipping that survives only in quotation and idiom.
entries.example: ויהי אור. — And there was light.

entries.label: Pronouns
entries.usage: אתה/את and הוא/היא — gender is marked on everything but I and we.
entries.example: היא אישה טובה. — She is a good woman.

entries.label: Definite article
entries.usage: One letter glued to the front; there is no word for a or an.
entries.example: הבית גדול. — The house is big.

entries.label: Adjective gender
entries.usage: The feminine usually adds ה־: טוב becomes טובה.
entries.example: האישה טובה. — The woman is good.

entries.label: Plural agreement
entries.usage: ים־ and ות־ on the noun, and the adjective copies both gender and number.
entries.example: המחברות גדולות. — The notebooks are big.

entries.label: Numbers
entries.usage: Two counting sets; the forms ending in ה are the masculine ones.
entries.example: יש לי שלושה ספרים. — I have three books.

entries.label: Possession של
entries.usage: The easy possessive: הבית של דוד.
entries.example: הבית של דוד. — The house is David's.

entries.label: יש לי (have)
entries.usage: No verb to have — יש plus a to-form does the job, אין for the negative.
entries.example: יש לנו כלב. — We have a dog.

entries.label: Preposition endings
entries.usage: The preposition swallows its pronoun: לי, לך, לו, אצלי.
entries.example: הוא נתן לי ספר. — He gave me a book.

entries.label: Smichut
entries.usage: Two nouns side by side; only the last one takes the article.
entries.example: אכלתי עוגת שוקולד. — I ate a chocolate cake.

entries.label: Verbal nouns
entries.usage: One action-noun shape per binyan: כתיבה, דיבור, הסבר.
entries.example: הליכה היא ספורט טוב. — Walking is good exercise.

entries.label: Long chains
entries.usage: Three nouns deep, adjective only at the end: משרד ראש הממשלה.
entries.example: הוא עובד במשרד ראש הממשלה. — He works in the Prime Minister's Office.

entries.point: No verb "to be" in the present tense
entries.label: Zero copula
entries.usage: Subject and predicate sit side by side, with no is or are.
entries.example: הבית גדול. — The house is big.

entries.label: Negation
entries.usage: לא goes straight in front of the verb or adjective.
entries.example: הוא לא הולך. — He isn't going.

entries.label: יש / אין
entries.usage: There is and there isn't, the base of the possession pattern too.
entries.example: יש בית גדול. — There is a big house.

entries.label: Questions
entries.usage: Statement word order plus intonation; מה, מי, איפה, מתי, למה lead.
entries.example: איפה אתה גר? — Where do you live?

entries.label: Object marker את
entries.usage: Flags a definite direct object; untranslatable, and never optional.
entries.example: אני רואה את הבית. — I see the house.

entries.point: Object pronouns and their literary suffixed forms
entries.label: Object pronouns
entries.usage: אותי, אותו, אותם in speech; ראיתיו and its kin in print.
entries.example: פגשנו אותם אתמול. — We met them yesterday.

entries.label: Relative ש־
entries.usage: One prefix for who, which and that — and it can never be dropped.
entries.example: האיש שגר כאן הוא רופא. — The man who lives here is a doctor.

entries.label: Comparison
entries.usage: יותר ... מ־ for more than, הכי for the top of the class.
entries.example: דן גבוה יותר מדנה. — Dan is taller than Dana.

entries.label: Conditionals (אם)
entries.usage: A condition that may come true — future tense in both halves.
entries.example: אם ירד גשם, נישאר בבית. — If it rains, we'll stay home.

entries.point: Temporal clauses: כש־, לפני ש־, אחרי ש־
entries.label: Time clauses
entries.usage: Preposition plus ש־ before a clause; the ש drops before a plain noun.
entries.example: אכלתי לפני שיצאתי מהבית. — I ate before I left the house.

entries.point: Unreal conditionals with אילו and לו
entries.label: Counterfactuals
entries.usage: אילו or לו with היה plus a present participle in both halves.
entries.example: אילו היה לי זמן, הייתי בא. — If I had time, I would come.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: ש־ is obligatory, and the original tense is kept, not shifted back.
entries.example: הוא אמר שהוא עייף. — He said that he was tired.

entries.label: Register
entries.usage: אולם, בשל, בלבד in writing where speech says אבל, בגלל, רק.
entries.example: הכניסה למנויים בלבד. — Entry for subscribers only.

entries.label: Relative אשר
entries.usage: The free-standing relative of written Hebrew, especially before a preposition.
entries.example: הנושא אשר עליו דיברנו חשוב. — The topic we spoke about is important.

entries.label: Register switching
entries.usage: בטרם and אין ב־ ... כדי beside quoted ש־, כי and בגלל.
entries.example: בטרם יצאנו, בדקנו את הכתובת. — Before we left, we checked the address.
